why: THE CENSUS OF EVERYTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT PHOTOGRAPHS THE FRAMEBUFFER.
Three tools have now shipped that photographed something other than the thing
they were named for — a sprite suite reading its own cache, a frame lab that
graded 24 pictures of the main menu, and a --ui-tour that photographed the same
menu eleven more times while it ate every key the tour pressed. Each was found
by a human holding two PNGs side by side.
tests/gate/test_screenshot_guards.gd reads this file. The rule it enforces is
short: a file that reads the framebuffer must name LcnShutter (tools/ui_tour_shutter.gd),
or carry both guards inline and be listed under `guarded_inline` with the
functions that hold them, or be listed under `blind` as named debt. A file in
none of the three is RED — so a NEW screenshot tool cannot be born blind, and
the only way to add one that is, is to write a row here on purpose.
The two guards, both of which the frame lab learned the hard way:
CHROME  nothing may be drawn above the subject when the shutter opens
DIFF    photographs of different things must actually differ

guarded_inline.photographs: the art direction matrix — six hours by five zooms, plus the night, the crowd, the weather and the ground's memory
guarded_inline.note: Where both guards were invented. It strips to LcnLayers.POST and fingerprints every cell; --keep-chrome shows them going red. Left inline on purpose: it is [P13]'s file, and this suite asserts the two functions still exist rather than reaching into another part's folder to rewrite them.

blind.photographs: the HUD in each of its three compositions
blind.cost: a shot taken with a modal or a story card over the clock plate grades the card

blind.photographs: the production graphs and the night report
blind.cost: same class: nothing asserts the statistics screen is the thing in the frame

blind.photographs: particle plates, with and without the effects layer
blind.cost: it is already a differential, so DIFF is half-present; CHROME is not asserted at all

blind.photographs: the juice gallery — shakes, flashes, impulses
blind.cost: no strip and no fingerprint; a full-screen layer would be graded as feel
it strips, but nothing compares its plates for being the same picture

blind.photographs: the title, pause, settings and save screens
blind.cost: it fingerprints, but nothing asserts what is above the screen it opened

blind.photographs: belts, arms and items in flight
blind.cost: no chrome assertion and no pairwise comparison

blind.photographs: a debug capture of the palette and browsers, on demand
blind.cost: same class as the tour's, in the part the tour photographs
lower stakes and the same defect: the thumbnail is grabbed while a menu is open, so every save in the browser is a picture of the save browser

misnamed_beats_why: tests/gate/test_shot_beats.gd asserts that every photographic beat in every
shipped scenario is taken in the phase and on the day its NAME claims. These
are the beats that cannot be: the scenario never reaches the moment it named,
so there is no tick to move the shot to. The harness refuses to photograph
them at all rather than write a PNG with a false name in it.
Every row is a one-line fix in a file this part does not own, so it is listed
instead of silently tolerated: named, owned, dated to this wave, and asserted
to still be true. A row that stops being true is RED, and the list may not
grow — a new misnamed beat has to displace one of these.

misnamed_beats.fix: smoke is 600 ticks and a run begins at ClimateProfile.opening_tick (2016), which is morning; the scenario scripts skip_to_phase for the other five phases and not for this one. Either add {"tick":20,"cmd":{"system":"climate","op":"skip_to_phase","phase":"dawn"}} before the shot, or rename the beat to what it actually shows.
